answer: Anchor each agent identity to one non-transferable, hardware-backed credential issued only after a costly stake check, so a single operator cannot mint a thousand cheap personas. Peers keep an atlas of these anchors, a public signed registry mapping every credential to its history, and only identities with a long consistent record earn trust. The rule is as strict as a sonnet's fixed form: no matching anchor, no seat at the table. Forging a new identity costs real money and time, so a Sybil flood becomes uneconomic while an honest newcomer can still join by paying the same price once.
